title: Average Height of Buildings in Each Segment
summary: A straight street is modeled by a number line with buildings represented as segments.
statement: A straight street is modeled by a number line with buildings represented as segments. Buildings are given as [start, end, height]. The task is to describe the street with the least number of non-overlapping segments, each with an average height. For instance, if buildings are at [1,5,2] and [3,10,4], the street can be described as [1,3,2], [3,5,3], [5,10,4]. Each segment's average height is calculated by dividing the total height by the number of buildings, and no segment includes areas without buildings. The output can be in any order, and a segment [a, b) includes a but not b.
constraints: buildings has up to 100000 [start,end,height] triples describing half-open intervals.
For each covered region use integer division of total active height by active building count.
Omit uncovered regions and merge adjacent regions with equal average height.
hints: Only building endpoints can change the active count or total height.
Sweep sorted endpoints with count and height deltas; emit the preceding interval from the old active state.
At each point emit [previous,point,total//count] when covered, then apply deltas; merge equal adjacent averages.
The active set is constant between consecutive endpoints, so every emitted average is exact and merging preserves the minimum-segment representation.
editorial: The active set is constant between consecutive endpoints, so every emitted average is exact and merging preserves the minimum-segment representation.

tests.explanation: The averages are two on [1,3), three on [3,4), and four on [4,9).
Adjacent elementary intervals with equal averages merge into [1,3,2] and [3,8,3].
